title: Independent source selection (foundational)
description: Signature original: The checker gathers candidate sources and first filters for independence: sources that cite each other or share an author are collapsed into one, because three copies of the same press release are not three independent confirmations. Independence is estimated from citation graphs and shared distinctive phrasing. Only sources passing this filter vote on the claim. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
sources = [{'id':'s1','cites':['s2']},{'id':'s2','cites':[]},{'id':'s3','cites':[]},{'id':'s4','cites':['s1']},{'id':'s5','cites':[]},]
indep = [s['id'] for s in sources if not s['cites']]
print('independent sources:', indep, '(collapsed', len(sources)-len(indep), 'derivative)')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Cross-Source Fact Checker, 2026-10-21.

title: Claim normalization for comparison (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before comparison, claims are normalized: numbers are converted to a canonical unit, dates to ISO format, and entity names lowercased and stripped of titles. Normalization prevents false conflicts like '52,000' versus '52 thousand' or 'Oct 21' versus '2026-10-21'. The normalized form is what gets compared across sources. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import re
def norm(s):
    s = s.lower()
    s = re.sub(r'(\d+),(\d+)', r'\1\2', s)
    s = s.replace(' thousand', '000').replace('oct ', '10-')
    return s
print(norm('52,000 databases'))
print(norm('52 thousand databases'))
print('match:', norm('52,000 databases') == norm('52 thousand databases'))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Cross-Source Fact Checker, 2026-10-21.

title: Weighted majority verdict (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each independent source casts a vote of confirm, deny, or unknown on the normalized claim, weighted by that source's historical reliability score. The verdict is the weighted majority; a claim confirmed by high-reliability sources outranks one confirmed only by low-reliability ones. Ties and near-ties produce an 'unresolved' verdict rather than a false certainty. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
votes = [('s1','confirm',0.9),('s2','confirm',0.7),('s3','deny',0.4),('s4','unknown',0.5)]
w = {'confirm':0,'deny':0}
for _, v, rel in votes: w[v] = w.get(v,0) + rel
print('weighted votes:', {k: round(v,2) for k,v in w.items()})
print('verdict:', max(w, key=w.get) if max(w.values()) > sum(w.values())/2 else 'unresolved')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Cross-Source Fact Checker, 2026-10-21.

title: Conflict flagging with evidence pairs (foundational)
description: Signature original: When sources disagree, the checker emits a conflict record pairing the strongest confirming passage with the strongest denying passage, verbatim. Presenting both sides with their sources lets a human or downstream agent adjudicate instead of trusting a black-box verdict. The conflict record also notes which source attributes differ, such as publication date or measurement method. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
conflict = {'claim': 'archive count', 'confirm': ('srcA', '52,268 databases, verified Oct 20'), 'deny': ('srcB', '51,900 databases, estimated Sep 1')}
print('CONFLICT on:', conflict['claim'])
print(' +', conflict['confirm'])
print(' -', conflict['deny'])
print('note: dates differ -> re-check the newer source first')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Cross-Source Fact Checker, 2026-10-21.

t: Runtime verdict caching with source-version keys (foundational)
title: Runtime verdict caching with source-version keys (foundational)
description: Signature original: Verdicts are cached, but the cache key includes the version identifiers of every source consulted, so a verdict never outlives its evidence. If any source publishes a new version, the key changes and the claim is re-checked automatically. This keeps operational fact-checking fresh without re-running expensive comparisons on every request. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
cache = {}
def key(claim, srcvers): return claim + '|' + ','.join(sorted(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in srcvers.items()))
k1 = key('count=52268', {'srcA':'v3','srcB':'v1'})
cache[k1] = 'confirmed'
k2 = key('count=52268', {'srcA':'v4','srcB':'v1'})  # srcA updated
print('cache hit after source update:', k2 in cache, '-> re-check required')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Cross-Source Fact Checker, 2026-10-21.
